observation.description: The secrets-and-config guide names the config operations (status, set, unset, verify) but shows them only through the repo kit's configApi helper, which a public consumer does not have; neither the routes nor the request shapes are documented. The arm recovered them by probing: GET /_snapback/api/config/status (admin token), POST /_snapback/api/config/set with {entry: <name>, value: <string>} (a nested-object spelling 422s with a serde error naming the missing field, and {entry, member} 400s with SNAPBACK_CONFIG_VALUE_INVALID 'provide exactly one of value or values'), POST /_snapback/api/config/unset with {entry}. The custody behavior itself is excellent once reached (status reports set/secret/memberCount and never bytes; set returns {applyState:'applied', generation}).

competitorOutcome.description: Convex documents `npx convex env set NAME value` and the dashboard flow as the first-class consumer path for deployment config. Longitudinal repeat: the 0102-epoch Snapback Partiful arm recorded the same gap ('local config automation named the operations without a runnable request shape') and filed a guide-gap ticket; the shapes are still undocumented on 0.1.7.

mustNotRegress: Values never appearing in status output, manifests, or seed data; the admin-gated custody boundary.
smallestCoherentFix: A guide subsection (or CLI verbs: snapback config status|set|unset) giving the exact routes, header, and body shapes a public consumer can call, with the {entry, value}/{entry, values} union spelled out.
acceptanceWitness: A consumer following only the guide sets, verifies, and unsets a config entry against a dev server without reading package or binary internals; a guide check exercises the documented shapes.
